questions.prompt: The soldiers were about to burst into the walls of the city when a storm arose.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs in moenia urbis irruptūrī erant, cum tempestās coorta est.

questions.prompt: We must praise justice, although the powerful hate it.
questions.answer: Nōbīs aequitās laudanda est, etsī potentēs eam ōdērunt.

questions.prompt: The rustic old man was about to speak, but astonishment held his tongue.
questions.answer: Agrestis senex locūtūrus erat, sed stupor linguam tenēbat.

questions.prompt: This spectacle must be watched tomorrow by all the citizens.
questions.answer: Hoc spectāculum crās omnibus cīvibus spectandum est.

questions.prompt: The general was about to lead the legions across the river at first light.
questions.answer: Dux legiōnēs prīmā lūce trāns flūmen ductūrus erat.

questions.prompt: Your promises must be kept, lest you lose the trust of your friends.
questions.answer: Prōmissa tibi servanda sunt, nē amīcōrum fidem āmittās.

questions.prompt: I shall be about to set out for Greece when the winter has ended.
questions.answer: In Graeciam profectūrus erō, cum hiems fīnīta erit.

questions.prompt: May I be about to die bravely, defending my homeland.
questions.answer: Fortiter moritūrus sim, patriam dēfendēns.

questions.prompt: These letters ought to have been sent long ago.
questions.answer: Hae litterae iam prīdem mittendae fuērunt.

questions.prompt: The poet, about to sing of ancient wars, invoked the Muse.
questions.answer: Poēta, dē antīquīs bellīs cantātūrus, Mūsam invocāvit.

questions.prompt: This wine must not be drunk by the sick man.
questions.answer: Hoc vīnum aegrōtō nōn bibendum est.

questions.prompt: The consul, about to address the crowd, climbed the rostra.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, turbam adlocūtūrus, rōstra cōnscendit.

questions.prompt: Great honors are to be given to those who have deserved them.
questions.answer: Magnī honōrēs iīs dandī sunt quī eōs meruērunt.

questions.prompt: The messenger announced that the walls were going to fall.
questions.answer: Nūntius moenia cāsūra esse nūntiāvit.

questions.prompt: The anger of the gods ought to have been feared by you, foolish man.
questions.answer: Deōrum īra tibi timenda fuit, stulte.

questions.prompt: The maiden, about to be married, was weaving garlands of flowers.
questions.answer: Virgō, nūptūra, corōnās flōrum nectēbat.

questions.prompt: This difficult task must be undertaken by us with courage.
questions.answer: Hoc difficile opus nōbīs cum virtūte suscipiendum est.

questions.prompt: The old man said that he was about to leave everything to his sons.
questions.answer: Senex sē omnia fīliīs relictūrum esse dīxit.

questions.prompt: The truth had to be told, however bitter it was.
questions.answer: Vērum dīcendum erat, quamvīs amārum esset.

questions.prompt: The old man, about to set out, entrusted his fields to his sons.
questions.answer: Senex, profectūrus, agrōs suōs fīliīs mandāvit.

questions.prompt: This letter must be written before nightfall.
questions.answer: Haec epistula ante noctem scrībenda est.

questions.prompt: We were about to praise the poet when he suddenly fell silent.
questions.answer: Poētam laudātūrī erāmus cum subitō conticuit.

questions.prompt: The bridge had to be destroyed lest the enemy cross.
questions.answer: Pōns dēlendus erat nē hostēs trānsīrent.

questions.prompt: The queen, about to flee the besieged city, hid her jewels.
questions.answer: Rēgīna, ex urbe obsessā fugitūra, gemmās suās cēlāvit.

questions.prompt: These laws must be obeyed by all the citizens.
questions.answer: Hīs lēgibus ab omnibus cīvibus pārendum est.

questions.prompt: I shall be about to set sail when the winds have risen.
questions.answer: Nāvigātūrus erō cum ventī surrēxerint.

questions.prompt: The general knew that the camp had to be defended at all costs.
questions.answer: Dux sciēbat castra omnīnō dēfendenda esse.

questions.prompt: The soldiers, about to storm the walls, were sharpening their swords in silence.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, moenia oppugnātūrī, gladiōs suōs silentiō acuēbant.

questions.prompt: This bitterness of soul must be endured by the wise man with patience.
questions.answer: Haec animī amāritūdō sapientī patienter ferenda est.

questions.prompt: The barren fields had to be plowed again before the seeds were sown.
questions.answer: Sterilēs agrī iterum arandī erant antequam sēmina sererentur.

questions.prompt: We were about to free the captives when the trumpet suddenly sounded.
questions.answer: Captīvōs līberātūrī erāmus cum subitō tuba cecinit.

questions.prompt: These sacred rites must be performed by the priest before dawn.
questions.answer: Hī sacrī rītūs ā sacerdōte ante lūcem faciendī sunt.

questions.prompt: The queen was about to entrust her innumerable treasures to a faithful servant.
questions.answer: Rēgīna innumerābilēs thēsaurōs suōs fidēlī servō commissūra erat.

questions.prompt: This false rumor ought to have been scattered by a single true word.
questions.answer: Hic falsus rūmor ūnō vērō verbō discutiendus fuit.

questions.prompt: The consul, about to assign the provinces, summoned the senators to the curia.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, prōvinciās assignātūrus, senātōrēs in cūriam vocāvit.

questions.prompt: Let the temple, about to fall into ruin, be restored by pious hands.
questions.answer: Templum, in ruīnam cāsūrum, piīs manibus restituātur.

questions.prompt: The general said that the camp would have to be moved before nightfall.
questions.answer: Dux castra ante noctem movenda esse dīxit.

questions.prompt: You ought to have beseeched the gods, foolish man, before you began the war.
questions.answer: Deī tibi, stulte, precandī fuērunt antequam bellum inchoārēs.

questions.prompt: The soldiers were about to endure innumerable hardships in the barren mountains.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs innumerābilēs labōrēs in sterilibus montibus passūrī erant.

questions.prompt: This modest maiden is to be praised by all on account of her virtue.
questions.answer: Haec modesta virgō ab omnibus propter virtūtem laudanda est.

questions.prompt: The farmer, about to sow the fields, was watching the rising stars.
questions.answer: Agricola, agrōs sēminātūrus, surgentēs stēllās spectābat.

questions.prompt: The bridge must be raised quickly, lest the river carry it away.
questions.answer: Pōns celeriter ērigendus est, nē eum flūmen auferat.

questions.prompt: I was about to break my silence when the harsh judge ordered me to be quiet.
questions.answer: Silentium meum ruptūrus eram cum dūrus iūdex mē tacēre iussit.

questions.prompt: This tongue of yours must be cut out by you, and even when it has been torn out, with my very breath my freedom will refute your lust.
questions.answer: Haec tibi est incīdenda lingua, quā vel ēvulsā spīritū ipsō libīdinem tuam lībertās mea refūtābit.

questions.prompt: One had to come to them, against Apronius — men who had not yet breathed off the drunkenness of the Apronian banquet.
questions.answer: Veniendum erat ad eōs contrā Aprōnium qui nōndum Aprōniānī conviviī crāpulam exhālassent.

questions.prompt: These things, when they ought to be present, must then be so arranged and varied that they charm the hearer with every sound, as we see happens in the strings of a lyre.
questions.answer: Quae cum adesse dēbent, tum disponenda atque varianda sunt, ut audītōrem, quod in fidibus fierī vidēmus, omnī sonō mulceant.

questions.prompt: But if there is any fear of unpopularity, the unpopularity of sternness and courage is not to be dreaded more strongly than that of idleness and worthlessness.
questions.answer: Sed, sī quis est invidiae metus, nōn est vehementius sevēritātis ac fortitūdinis invidiā quam inertiae ac nēquitiae pertimēscenda.

questions.prompt: What pleasures, then, of banquets or games or harlots are to be compared with these pleasures?
questions.answer: Quae sunt igitur epulārum aut lūdōrum aut scortōrum voluptātēs cum hīs voluptātibus comparandae?

questions.prompt: The highest safety of the state must not too often be risked on one man.
questions.answer: Nōn est saepius in ūnō homine summā salūs perīclitanda reī pūblicae.

questions.prompt: A grave and intolerable wrong has been done.
questions.answer: Gravis iniūria facta est et nōn ferenda.

questions.prompt: Will not the thing have to be agitated?
questions.answer: Nōn agitanda rēs erit?

questions.prompt: He had the temple of Castor to take care of.
questions.answer: Aedem Castoris habuit tuendam.

questions.prompt: With this kind of cavalry are you going to fight.
questions.answer: cum hōc equite pugnātūrī estis.

questions.prompt: Whatever is destined to be, will be.
questions.answer: fīet illud, quod futūrum est.
